column1: # Copy to your analysis folder, edit, and pass to epicc:
# Lines starting with '#' are skipped, so you can park samples without
#   Assay        ChIP | CUT_RUN | CUT_TAG | ATAC | RNAseq | RAMPAGE |
#                sRNA | WGBS | WGBS_nd | PBAT | EMseq | dmC
#   Genome       Reference genome name (must match `genomes:` key in the
#                options YAML). Comma-separate to map the same reads to
#                several references (e.g. ColCEN,TAIR10): reads are downloaded
#                and trimmed once, then aligned to each, and post-alignment
#                files are tagged with the genome. Must not contain '__'.
#                All rows in the sheet must use the same factor keys.
#   Read_files   SRA/ENA/DDBJ accession (SRR12345), local FASTQ/BAM path,
#                HTTP(S) URL, or '+'-separated list to merge multiple inputs.
#                For PE FASTQs at explicit paths: comma-separate R1,R2.
#   IP_target    Required for ChIP / CUT_RUN / CUT_TAG (H3K9me2, Input, WCE,
#   Control      Sample_ID of the matching control (Input/WCE for ChIP).
#                Control samples themselves leave this blank.
#   Peak_type    broad | narrow — the peak-calling type, a separate parameter
#                from the assay. Required for ChIP / CUT_RUN / CUT_TAG (broad
#                for histone domains like H3K9me2/H3K27me3; narrow for TFs and
#                sharp marks like H3K4me3/H3K27ac). Blank for all other assays.
#                Applies to only three assays, so it sits near the end.
#   Comments     Optional free text for your own notes (batch, library prep,
#                sequencing run, anything). Completely ignored by the pipeline —
#                it never affects analysis names or outputs. Last column.
# See dev/docs/sample-sheet-spec.md for the full per-field specification
# and tools/epicc-builder.html for an interactive editor.
